title: Amazon Redshift
description: An Amazon Redshift cluster or Serverless workgroup, read with a user that may only read.

fields.name: host
fields.label: Endpoint
fields.help: Paste the Endpoint as the Redshift console shows it (or its JDBC URL): the port and database in it are used.

fields.name: database
fields.label: Database
fields.help: The one the endpoint names, else dev.

fields.name: ssl
fields.label: SSL
fields.help: require (the default) for anything on a network.

fields.name: schemas
fields.label: Schemas
fields.help: Which schemas to read (comma-separated); every schema the user may see when empty.

setup.title: Where the cluster is
setup.say:
Paste the Endpoint from the Redshift console — a provisioned cluster: Clusters → your cluster → General information → Endpoint; Serverless: Workgroup configuration → your workgroup → Endpoint. The port and database in it are taken from it.

The engine must be able to reach it: the cluster (or workgroup) publicly accessible, or the engine in the same network, and its security group letting the engine's address in on port 5439.

fix.say: No computer answers to that name. Copy the Endpoint again from the Redshift console; a cluster that is not publicly accessible has no address outside its own network.

Nothing came back: Redshift's security group is dropping the connection. Add an inbound rule to it — Custom TCP, port 5439, from the engine's address — and make the cluster (or workgroup) publicly accessible if the engine is outside its network.

setup.title: A user that may only read
setup.say: Superatom only reads, and reads in read-only transactions. Give it a user of its own that may read and nothing more — run this as an admin, in the database to read (choose a password: 8 to 64 characters, with an upper-case letter, a lower-case letter and a digit):

copy.label: Make a read-only user

fix.say: Redshift refused the user name or the password. Check both (the user name is lower-case unless it was made in quotes), or set a new password: ALTER USER {user} PASSWORD '…';
There is no database {database} in this cluster. The first database of a cluster is usually dev — give the one your tables are in.

setup.title: Which schemas
setup.say: Leave it empty to read every schema the user may see, or name the ones to read (public, sales). The check counts the tables it may read there.

fix.say: Signed in, but {user} may read no table there. Give it USAGE on the schemas and SELECT on their tables (the commands in the step before), or name a schema it may read.
